key_insight: Organic semiconductor performance in solar cells is strongly shaped by weak intermolecular forces and interface-driven supramolecular order, so controlling assembly can improve electronic behavior.
engineering_relevance: For organic photovoltaics, interface engineering and molecular orientation are practical design levers to make device performance more predictable and potentially more efficient.
method: Review of recent advances in organic-semiconductor interface assembly
Focus on supramolecular order and orientational anisotropy
Includes insights from computer simulations and device studies
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a survey of recent research across transistors, LEDs, and photovoltaics rather than reporting new experimental data or a single benchmark result.
watch_item: Device outcomes are still hard to predict from chemical structure alone, and simulation/modeling of disordered interfaces remains challenging.
paper_title: The interplay of interfaces, supramolecular assembly, and electronics in organic semiconductors
